remaining_concerns: The record still does not support clean certification without material caveats under the stated policy.
No approved mitigation is in evidence for the Spanish-language billing weakness; the draft runbook still lacks required policy elements such as owner and acceptance threshold.
The model-card draft language stating there are no known material limitations remains inconsistent with the live Spanish billing limitation unless that disclosure is corrected.
The caveated position depends on explicit disclosure and deployment monitoring, but final approved disclosure language and final governance artifacts are not in evidence.
No admissible evidence was provided showing the Spanish-language billing weakness is no longer material or formally approved as mitigated.
final_rationale: The actor did not provide new admissible evidence. The audit picture changed only because the actor abandoned the overbroad clean-certification position and narrowed the claim to a caveated, policy-bounded one that is materially more consistent with the existing record. On the available summary, aggregate readiness and a clean rehearsal are positive evidence, and public guidance supports documenting limitations and monitoring risk in deployment. But the policy text is explicit that certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation containing the required elements, and that predicate is still unmet. The supportable conclusion from the admissible record is therefore not clean compliance, but a caveated compliance posture only if the Spanish-language billing limitation is explicitly disclosed and monitored rather than omitted. This is a proportional update based on a narrower interpretation of the same evidence, not on any new proof.
